claims.statement: Tom Allen settled in St. Louis in the 1860s and brought a good fighting reputation with him.
claims.excerpt: St. Louis in the sixties and brought with him a pretty good fighting reputation

claims.statement: Tom Allen was the only St. Louis fighter living here to claim a world title and gain partial recognition as champion.
claims.excerpt: to claim the title and gain at least partial recognition as a world champion

claims.statement: Tom Allen was the proprietor of a saloon on Market Street east of Seventh.
claims.excerpt: proprietor of a saloon on Market street east of Seventh
places: Market Street east of Seventh, St. Louis

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Mike McCoole in 1869 and won in the ring, but the referee gave the decision to McCoole.
claims.excerpt: Although Allen won the fight, the referee, intimidated by Mc-Coole’s backers

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Mike McCoole in seven rounds on an island in the Mississippi, regaining the title.
claims.excerpt: Allen cut McCoole to ribbons in seven rounds

claims.statement: Joe Goss beat Tom Allen, who had held the title until then.
claims.excerpt: He held it until beaten by Joe Goss

claims.statement: After retiring, Tom Allen renamed his saloon Champion's Rest, the name it kept for many years.
claims.excerpt: to the one it carried for many years

claims.statement: Tom Allen's place had a large back room with a ring pitched in one corner and a platform for a piano in another.
claims.excerpt: included a large back room with a ring pitched in one corner

claims.statement: Tom Allen sat by the doorway with a gavel as master of ceremonies and bouncer.
claims.excerpt: acted as master of ceremonies or, if need be, bouncer

claims.statement: At Allen's place, disputants who got too noisy were thrown into the ring with gloves on and told to fight it out.
claims.excerpt: they were thrown into the ring, hands gloved and told to fight it out

claims.statement: Tom Allen died in 1904 (the article's date; other articles give 1903).
claims.excerpt: Tom died in 1904 and the “Champion's Rest” passed out
